claim: For every preference datum, DPO and KL-regularized RLHF optimize equivalent objectives if and only if the RLHF-optimal policy prefers the human-preferred response; equivalently, delta_ref > -reward_gap / beta for every pair.

quantifiers.dataset: all ordered preference triples (x, y_w, y_l) in D
quantifiers.parameters: all beta > 0 and reward_gap = r*(y_w) - r*(y_l) > 0

assumptions: The policy assigns positive probability to both responses so log odds are finite.
The RLHF optimum obeys delta_star = delta_ref + reward_gap / beta.
The DPO objective is the ordered-pair loss stated by the paper: -log sigma(beta * (delta - delta_ref)).
falsification_rule: FALSIFIED if one valid finite-policy instance satisfies every premise and the boundary condition while the RLHF optimum is not a DPO optimum.
limitations: This contract tests the theorem exactly as written for the ordered-pair DPO loss. It does not test a different population cross-entropy that averages both possible stochastic labels for the same pair.
